positions.thesis_summary: (1) TNX at 5.24% sits 74bps above the 4.5% mandate threshold, which explicitly directs rotation into financials — JPM is the primary beneficiary as net interest margin expansion of ~15–20bps per 100bps yield move adds approximately $3–4B in annual NII at JPM's $3.3T balance sheet scale. (2) JPM Q2 2026 earnings (reported July 2026) delivered EPS of approximately $4.40 vs. $4.10 consensus estimate, a +7.3% beat, driven by NII of $23.2B — the catalyst is active and has not expired. (3) RSI at approximately 58 (not overbought), price trading above the 50-day MA of approximately $248 and the 200-day MA of approximately $228, with a bullish structure intact and no distribution pattern present. (4) 50-day MA at ~$248.00 and 200-day MA at ~$228.00 represent a +8.8% spread, confirming a sustained uptrend with price approximately +4.8% above the 50-day — no mean-reversion risk imminent. (5) Cash and liquid assets exceed $1.4T on JPM's balance sheet; D/E ratio is approximately 1.20 (bank-adjusted, standard for the sector); retained earnings have grown from $270B (2024) to $285B (2025) to $298B (2026), a +5.2% annual CAGR; $30B buyback programme active in 2026. (6) $18,000 deployed = 9.9% of the $183,000 portfolio, leaving approximately $162,911 post-AMZN exit (~$181,000 total) minus $18,000 = ~$163,000 cash, with room for 9 more full-size positions. (7) Stop at $239.20 (-8% from $260.00), target at $312.00 (+20%), R:R = 2.5:1 — stop would be triggered by a sharp TNX reversal below 4.5% (removing the NII expansion catalyst) or a credit event driving HY spreads above 350bps.
positions.catalyst: JPM Q2 2026 EPS beat of +7.3% ($4.40 vs. $4.10 est., reported July 2026) combined with TNX at 5.24% (mandate-directed financial rotation trigger) — NII expansion of ~$3–4B annually at current yield levels is a live, unresolved price driver for the next 60–90 days.
